Revised assessment using Beige Book insights: The FOMC statement’s balance of robust job gains and elevated inflation is tempered by the Beige Book’s broad-based signs of slowing. Across several districts, overall activity was flat to slightly down, consumer spending and manufacturing were mixed-to-softer, and labor-market tightness eased at the margin with moderating (but still elevated) wage growth. Price pressures showed some moderation but remained above target. Both the Beige Book and SLOOS point to tighter credit standards and weaker loan demand—especially in C&I and CRE—with particular vulnerability in office, construction/land development, and multifamily. These conditions reinforce the Committee’s expectation that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring, and they heighten downside risks to growth and credit quality. While policy implementation tools and ongoing runoff support market functioning, they do not offset the expected credit drag. Net tone: more cautious than prior; shift further into modestly negative.
